correctness.rationale: For non-scalar residue matrices the commuting-lift fiber has exactly q^(2d) elements above each residue centralizer element; for scalar residue matrices the residue common-centralizer criterion on d radical coefficients is exact. Two-by-two cyclic centralizers fall into three quadratic algebra types, whose embedded-algebra counts yield a disjoint partition of all q^(4d) coefficient tuples. The resulting eight rows exhaust |GL2(R)| and orbit-stabilizer yields the stated class number and exceptional-stratum complement. Direct full matrix-product enumerations for five finite test rings, including mixed characteristic, match all centralizer-size frequencies. Boundary q=2 and d=1 cases were checked and explicitly handled.

originality.rationale: The closest fully inspected work [1] proves a general orbit reduction for arbitrary radical-square-zero local rings (Theorem 10.3) and the principal d=1 GL2 count, but explicitly leaves nonprincipal tuple-orbit enumeration open as a calculation. The second closely relevant full text [2] counts pairwise-commuting field-matrix tuples only. The present exact nonprincipal eight-row centralizer census, full class number, and dominance of noncommuting radical coefficients are not stated there, and published-index searches located no dominating explicit formula. This is a best-knowledge priority assessment, not a proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: A general orbit classification in [1] already implies an algorithm for the concrete case; this assessment credits it fully and limits novelty to the evaluated weighted spectrum and its asymptotic.
An unindexed or inaccessible explicit nonprincipal GL2 conjugacy spectrum could predate this result.
Other published exact ring-theoretic formulas may specialize to the same centralizer census without matching the searched language.

value.rationale: The class-size spectrum is a fundamental, natural group invariant, strictly finer than a group order or total class number, for every finite local ring with square-zero maximal ideal. The theorem gives a uniform exact nonprincipal census across arbitrary embedding dimension and mixed characteristic, identifies the precise onset of the noncommuting deformation family at d=2, and proves it asymptotically dominates conjugacy classes. This resolves a motivated quantitative low-degree instance left unevaluated by the general extension-orbit framework, without asserting any broader theorem or independent certification.
